content: This medication is indicated for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC). The recommended dosage is 20 grams taken orally once daily. If persistent loose stools occur, the dosage should be reduced to 10 grams taken orally once daily. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been fully established. Post-marketing reports have also noted hypersensitivity reactions, such as rash and pruritus. This medication is contraindicated in individuals with known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction or galactosemia. There is insufficient data from case reports on its use in pregnant women to assess the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Additionally, there is no available data on the presence of lactitol in human or animal milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. When prescribing this medication to breastfeeding mothers, the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered alongside the mother’s clinical need for lactitol and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant or the underlying maternal condition. Lactitol is minimally absorbed in the small intestine. Any unabsorbed lactitol is expected to be degraded into organic acids in the colon and is minimally excreted in the feces. It is recommended to take this medication with meals. Oral medications should be administered at least two hours before or after taking lactitol to avoid interactions. The medication should be stored at a temperature of 20–25°C (68–77°F), with permissible excursions to 15–30°C (59–86°F).
